fields.title: Decide whether the flags store refuses a session whose search_path resolves into the flags schema

data.text: Found by the first hosted native-flags-postgres run (GitHub Actions run 42495859515, job 128778032913): the CI admin role was named flags, PostgreSQL 18's default search_path is "$user", public (docs §5.10.3), so once flags migrations create schema flags, an unqualified host name resolves into it. migrations.rs:146 host().run then read flags._sqlx_migrations and failed VersionMissing(20261106000000). Reproduced locally with a temporary role named flags (same failure), passes as any other role. The store's own queries are schema-qualified and unaffected. Hazard for applications: a login named flags (or SET ROLE flags) puts host unqualified tables and SQLx's default _sqlx_migrations ledger into the flags schema; a strict host migrator fails loudly, but one with set_ignore_missing(true) silently records its versions in the flags ledger and creates its tables there until the next strict flags migration fails. CI fixed by renaming the role ci_admin; documented in crates/batter-flags-postgres/README.md. Open question: should PooledStore::migrate (or registration) refuse when current_schemas(false) places flags first, or is it application policy (role naming / explicit search_path)? Evaluate per ADR-010.

Correction to the first comment: PooledStore::migrate sets set_ignore_missing(true) (src/migrate.rs:56), so host versions recorded in flags._sqlx_migrations by a host migrator that also ignores missing versions are never refused on the protected path; only the strict MIGRATOR refuses them. The misplacement is therefore silent indefinitely under the protected path, which raises the priority of a refusal.

Reproduced locally (PG 18.6, temporary superuser role named flags, dropped afterwards) with a throwaway test: after PooledStore::migrate, a host Migrator with set_ignore_missing(true) running CREATE TABLE host_data created it in schema flags and recorded version 1 in flags._sqlx_migrations; a second PooledStore::migrate returned Ok; MIGRATOR.run returned VersionMissing(1). PostgreSQL 18 docs §5.10.3 (ddl-schemas.html#DDL-SCHEMAS-PATH, fetched 2026-11-08): default search_path is "$user", public, and 'The first schema in the search path that exists is the default location for creating new objects.'

fields.title: Audit implicit state machines introduced on feat/flags-epic

data.text:
Read-only branch audit at ae6e4107196df61accf01436a7eaf42828e86bf3 against merge-base af4cb5638570cf98d0bbdddedeaf5bbf4b19a13a (origin/master...HEAD). Reviewed branch-added/changed runtime paths, searched changed sources and fixtures for distributed lifecycle state, and checked previous flags audit dispositions. No source edits, commits, or publication.

Findings:

1. P1 — Missing terminal interrupt state. crates/batter-flags-postgres/src/write.rs:186-192 polls Interrupt::On's oneshot using the Ok(()) pattern. If the sender is dropped, Err is consumed but On still retains the completed receiver. A committing preparation then reaches lines 224-234 and polls it again, panicking before COMMIT. The documented promise that sender drop interrupts nothing is broken. Model Armed/Disabled (or reuse Never on closure), consuming closure exactly once; a single fused owned interrupt future spanning both phases is another option. Executed an isolated reproduction of the two select/await phases using the locally compiled locked Tokio 1.54.1 artifact: preparation completed after sender drop, second poll panicked with called after complete, and catch_unwind confirmed the expected panic. This is a control-flow reproduction, not a live PostgreSQL integration run.

2. P2 — Registered-pool ownership is inferred, not proved. crates/batter-flags/src/control_plane.rs:124-135 claims ControlPlaneStore accepts only a pool with registered cleanup and therefore stop runs before pool close. PgProfiledPool carries only pool/profile and is also returned by batter_sqlx::low_level::connect_profiled_pool_lazy/connect_profiled_pool, which install no cleanup; even protected pool_in can use a different cleanup stack from register_in's target (lines 281-289). The canonical adapter cannot distinguish Unregistered, RegisteredElsewhere, or RegisteredHere. Require a registration-owner-bound pool capability or perform pool/flags registration together. Static API finding; no remote-liveness claim.

3. P2 — Persistence work selection precedes exclusive writer admission. crates/batter-flags/src/last_good/persist.rs:91-109 copies queue/written, then encodes, then acquires the semaphore. A prior timed-out blocking attempt can finish between those steps, advance Written::Never to At(v), clear the queue and release its permit. The next attempt still runs from the old selected work/first-write state. In particular it can skip the newer-file guard at lines 147-153 and overwrite another process's newer file. Waiting/selected/in-flight ownership is spread over the queue, historical Written value, semaphore and captured closure instead of one protected transition. Acquire the writer permit before selecting/revalidating state, and explicitly own the in-flight work. This interleaving is source-derived, not dynamically reproduced.

4. P2 — Presence preparation has an implicit cleanup-registration phase. crates/batter-flags/src/control_plane/presence.rs:208-228 exposes reserve_stop(&self,target) and register(self,target,...), with no proof linking them. Internal callers can omit reservation, register first, or use different targets. register_with currently calls them in the correct order (control_plane.rs:356-366), so no current failing public path is asserted for this separate finding. Make reservation consume Prepared and return the sole value that can register components, bound to the same target, or own both actions in one method. This directly violates the rule covering internal caller-enforced ordering.

5. P3 — Declaration construction's invalid/set-once state remains distributed. crates/batter-flags-core/src/builder/draft.rs:31-43 combines key: Result, error: Option, only_in: Option and governed_by: Option. The last two mean unset -> set -> poisoned on repetition (lines 122-157), while public setters return the same builder. finish resolves the state later. Other setters continue mutating after fail despite the comment saying later calls change nothing. This is representation/API debt, not proof an invalid Catalog escapes validation; the public repeated-setter residual is already disclosed in docs/evidence/api-assessments/flags.md:65-67. Use an explicit valid/invalid draft state and consuming set-once transitions or constructor-owned policy.

6. P3 — Encoding parser carries an implicit four-state protocol. crates/batter-flags-core/src/encoding.rs:84-115 tracks Empty / EncodingSeen / PayloadSeen / Complete via encoding_seen: bool plus payload: Option, with duplicate and completion transitions spread through the loop. Replace that pair with an exhaustive member-progress enum. Existing parser behavior passed its tests; this finding is compliance/maintainability, not a demonstrated decoding bug.

Other examined paths already use explicit state/proof types, including periodic wake/scheduling, authority/publication, row lifecycle, pending writes and acknowledged completion. Ordinary optional data and independent observations were not counted automatically as state machines. Immutable declaration Kind-plus-option payload representation is related invalid-state debt previously noted by the older audit, but not counted as a separate lifecycle finding here.

Verification: cargo test -p batter-flags-core --all-features --locked --lib encoding::tests passed all 4 tests on the pinned toolchain. Isolated Tokio receiver-reuse probe confirmed panic as above; temporary probe removed. Working tree remains clean. Full verify.sh was not run because this was a read-only audit with no code/dependency changes. No hosted CI or new Linux/live-PostgreSQL evidence claimed.

fields.title: Fix six implicit state protocols found on the flags branch

data.text: Implementation plan grounded in audit batter-jkw6.35: (1) own the interrupt wait across preparation/commit and test sender closure; (2) mint opaque cleanup-registration evidence in core, retain it in protected SQLx pools, and reject flags registration for foreign/unregistered pools before mutation; (3) make persistence selection an owned in-flight transition under one lock, with cancellation/drop retaining retry and completion evidence; (4) merge presence stop reservation and component registration under one internal owner; (5) model valid/invalid drafts explicitly and type the two set-once policies; (6) replace parser field-progress flags with an exhaustive enum. Steps 1/3/5/6 are independent; ownership evidence precedes flags registration validation. Preserve persisted formats and SQL migrations. Finish with API-surface/migration review, targeted regressions, then exactly one successful scripts/verify.sh run. Main risk is accidentally allowing stale cleanup evidence after take_cleanup; owner identity must move with the actual stack. No commit requested.

All six repairs are implemented. Interrupt now retains pending/requested/disabled states across both transaction phases; persistence atomically selects and owns a blocking write through completion or drop; opaque cleanup identity follows the actual stack and protected pools carry its receipt; presence consumes a stop reservation borrowing the same owner; draft rejection is absorbing and only_in/governed_by consume Unassigned policy types; parser member progress is exhaustive. Added independent regression and compile-fail coverage, updated guarantees/status/package guidance, and documented builder source compatibility cuts with no shim (a shim would restore repeated assignment). Targeted Clippy passed; all flags-core tests/doctests passed; flags family library tests passed; the dropped-sender live regression passed on local PostgreSQL 18.6. Public surface walker found 0 removed/4 added entries (2 marker enums plus reexports); reviewed setter and builder generic signature changes separately because the walker is name-only. Epic stays open: batter-jkw6.36 (six implicit-state repairs from audit batter-jkw6.35, including a P1 interrupt panic before COMMIT in batter-flags-postgres/src/write.rs) is in progress on feat/flags-epic and needs its own verify and a hosted run before PR #109 merges.

Design analysis (read-only; no code yet, because batter-jkw6.36 is editing batter-flags control_plane.rs and the flags-postgres crate in the shared checkout). (1) The store can only inspect its own sessions. Host migrators and application queries on other pools or logins stay application policy, so any refusal is partial and must say so. (2) Before the flags schema exists, current_schemas(false) omits it, even when search_path would resolve to it through "$user" or an explicit entry. Detecting this in PooledStore::migrate needs either a probe inside a rolled-back transaction (CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS flags, then test 'flags' = ANY(current_schemas(false)), then ROLLBACK), whose visibility on PG 18 must be verified, or parsing current_setting('search_path') with $user substitution, which is brittle. (3) After migration, control_plane::register_in and PooledStore::migrate can refuse with a plain 'flags' = ANY(current_schemas(false)) check. Note that any appearance of flags is hazardous, not only first place: a lookup of a name absent from public still falls through to flags. (4) Recommendation, per AGENTS.md's refuse-invalid-states policy: add a typed refusal in both places when the session's effective path includes flags. Name the role in the refusal and leave the search path out of it. Document other logins as application policy. This is additive within the unreleased flags family, but it newly refuses startups for a role named flags with the default path, which is the intent. It needs an ADR-010 assessment and a live test under a temporary role named flags. Implement it after batter-jkw6.36 lands to avoid conflicts.

data.text: Codex gpt-6-astra xhigh review of the uncommitted batter-jkw6.36 change (snapshot at ae6e4107 + working-tree diff): (P2) presence Reserved::registration returns &mut Registration<'a>, so an internal caller can replace the owner after the stop marker is reserved; (P2, pre-existing) Selected::finish ignores NotDurable, so a first write whose rename succeeded but directory sync failed keeps Written::Never and its retry can overwrite a newer file another process wrote; (P3) the persistence regression drives a hand-built Selected, not Persister::attempt's timeout/abandon path. Findings 1-6 otherwise assessed repaired; builder hard cuts meet the Breaking/Migration/no-shim rules.

Repairs in the scratch worktree (snapshot of the uncommitted batter-jkw6.36 change on ae6e4107): (1) presence Reserved::registration now returns a fresh Registration<'_> reborrow, not &mut to the stored owner; callers pass &mut presence.registration(). (2) Selected::finish records Err(NotDurable) as Written::At(version), since the rename already replaced the file, and keeps the snapshot queued for retry. (3) A cfg(test)-only one-shot hold on Persister lets a test abandon a write through Persister::attempt. New tests: an_unconfirmed_replacement_spends_the_first_write_so_its_retry_keeps_a_newer_file, an_unconfirmed_replacement_stays_queued_and_is_retried_over_its_own_file, a_write_the_deadline_abandons_through_attempt_holds_admission_and_records_its_outcome. Mutation checks: dropping the NotDurable record fails the first; dropping the Written record fails the third and the existing abandoned-write test. The removed observation/admission interleaving cannot be tested against the new code because selection and admission now share one critical section. batter-flags --features postgres lib: 95 passed. Clippy for batter-flags (no features, postgres, axum+runledger, all features) and fmt are clean. Docs updated: the assessment page, guarantees and the batter-flags AGENTS.md. A fresh Codex xhigh review of the full change is running.

Fresh Codex xhigh review of the full change: all six audit repairs plus the three repairs above assessed sound; one P3 remained, a test forcing the original selection/admission interleaving that fails under the old ordering. Added a cfg(test) pause right after selection, and the test an_attempt_during_an_in_flight_write_is_refused_before_it_can_hold_stale_history: with a write in flight, a second attempt must be refused (Busy) before the pause, and the newer file another process writes stays. Mutation check: reintroducing the old ordering (history captured before admission, pause between) fails it with left Ok(Written), right Err(Busy). While writing the test, the first version hung: a pause left armed after the expected Busy stopped the next attempt. The test now disarms it and bounds its awaits at 5 s. Persistence tests: 7 passed. Clippy (batter-flags: no features, postgres, axum+runledger, all features; forced re-check) and fmt are clean. Full verify.sh on the snapshot is running.

Implemented in the scratch worktree on da10b7de: ErrorClass::SearchPath. PooledStore::migrate inspects a pool session in the hardened read-only snapshot. PostgreSQL resolves the session default (pg_settings.reset_val, which DISCARD ALL restores) for one fully qualified statement through pg_catalog.current_schemas(false), and the hardened path is restored afterwards. The check runs before migrating, effective when the schema exists, and again after. A first attempt that read current_schemas inside the snapshot always passed, because the snapshot sets LOCAL search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp. Codex xhigh review round 1: (P2) the checks sample separate leases, so a pool whose connections logged in under different defaults can pass. Disposition: the claims are narrowed to sampled sessions. Inspecting the migrator's own connection would not close it, because flags statements are schema-qualified and the hazard lies in host sessions the store cannot enumerate. (P2) the StoreError and Deadline rustdoc promised nothing was written, which is false for migrate and was already false before this change, since SQLx commits each migration; fixed. (P3) the test did not prove the precheck; it now holds SQLx's migration advisory lock during the second call. Mutation checks: without the precheck the second call returns Database, not SearchPath; without the postcheck the first call succeeds; both fail the test. Live: store 42, loader 7, CLI 10, facade 16, all passed. A local run under a temporary role named flags was refused on both migrations; the role and two databases left by the panicked mutation runs were dropped. A fresh review is running.

Fresh Codex xhigh review round 2: no P1/P2; detection, temporary-path safety, ordering, the public API cut and the tests assessed sound. One P3: the sampling caveat named only role and database defaults, but PgPool::set_connect_options can also mix startup-option defaults within one pool. The caveat is broadened in the migrate rustdoc and comment, the README, guarantees and the assessment. Full verify.sh running.

fields.title: Audit implicit state machines in the flags public API (second pass)

data.text:
Read-only second-pass audit at 04627167 against merge-base af4cb563 (origin/master). Four parallel static reviews (flags-core; flags-postgres + CLI; flags control plane + last-good; flags reader/gates/facade/example) plus a direct read of the batter-core, batter-axum and batter-sqlx deltas. No code executed. The six batter-jkw6.35 findings are repaired and the repairs hold.

Implicit state machines / protocols in the public API, most severe first:

1. Publication lifecycle (batter_flags_core::low_level). Published has no unpublished state, so the loader keeps Option<Published> and chooses Published::first or next itself (batter-flags/src/reader.rs:330). first is public and callable at any time, bypassing Authority (accepts a regression). Candidate::carrying is an unenforced paired call that next never checks; omitting it releases a held engaged switch, breaking "holding never releases an engaged switch". next(&self) on a superseded clone derives from stale state. A refusal before the first publication is dropped (Writer::reject). The transition is split between control_plane/refresh.rs::publish (regression precheck, carrying) and reader.rs Writer::apply (first vs next, file age origin).
2. SnapshotStatus (batter_flags::control_plane) is a precedence enum folding loader liveness, what is served, and the latest read's verdict. Rejected/Regressed drop the served dimension; satisfies(Gate::Published) needs a second has_publication() read (status.rs:314); Published{Standing::Unpublished} maps to NotLoaded{ZERO}; Rejected.observed is always Some.
3. PooledStore::migrate: Resolution{Elsewhere, IntoFlags} folds "flags schema absent, cannot tell" into Elsewhere, so a first migration's pre-check always passes and the post-check can refuse after committing; Result<(), StoreError> cannot tell refused-before from refused-after-applying (tests/migrations.rs shows Err(SearchPath) with applied == 1).
4. Caller-ordered calls with no witness: declared::resolve must precede settings narrowing (silent defaults otherwise); PooledStore::preflight returns () and keys/key/history never check primary/schema themselves; low_level::gate_switch takes no proof that check_switch ran (foreign Released switch reads Open).
5. Gated periodic skip is core Ok(()) and counted in succeeded; skips live in a separate AtomicU64 outside the completion report.
6. RegisteredFlags::last_persist_failure is a sticky Option that never clears, not the persister's state.
7. Capabilities not bound to their issuer: ProcessPresence can be stopped against another store (Ok(NotRegistered)); LoadPolicy: Clone duplicates an opened SnapshotDirectory and first-write authority (plausible).
8. Smaller: Candidate.version Option + scope passed twice (runtime "structural corruption"); register_in not all-or-nothing (documented); with_listen defers a check it could make; CatalogBuilder::build empty vocabulary; dead variants BuildError::RepeatedCall, GateError::DeferOnWorkflowStep.

Adjacent ADR-010 items, not state machines: GateView<V>/AdmittedFlags compile outside a matching gated group and 500 per request; history silently capped at 1000 rows with no continuation; write accepts coordinated flips without recording it; pub mod test (TestFlags) ungated in production builds; serving grant set left to the caller; Flags::flagged under unready_until_loaded (plausible); SnapshotView::pin drops error decisions (plausible reach).

Clean: core PeriodicWake/SpacingGate/CadencePoint and ComponentState; CleanupRegistration + PgProfiledPool Cleanup enum (runtime pre-mutation refusal; residual: is_registered_in -> bool is an adapter obligation, take_cleanup after register_in); axum ResponseState, GroupPolicy constructors, Gated<V>; sqlx commit_unless/PgCommitStop, PgDeadlineError, migrate_until.

Residuals of the jkw6.36 repairs: persist State briefly (Writing, idle queue) -> spurious Busy; TooLarge encode stays queued; BuildError::RepeatedCall now unreachable.

Repairs for 1-3 split into child tasks of batter-jkw6.
